scenes.heading: Snowflake Virtual Warehouses & Scaling
scenes.narration: A virtual warehouse is Snowflake's unit of compute, and how you size and scale it drives both speed and cost.

scenes.heading: Warehouse fundamentals
bullets: T-shirt sizes from X-Small to 6X-Large double compute at each step.
Warehouses auto-suspend when idle so you stop paying instantly.
Auto-resume spins them back up the moment a query arrives.
Billing is per-second with a sixty-second minimum on resume.
scenes.narration: Each size up doubles the compute power and roughly the cost per hour. Auto-suspend stops billing the moment a warehouse goes idle, and auto-resume restarts it on demand. Per-second billing means you only pay for the time queries actually run.

scenes.heading: Scale up vs scale out
scenes.narration: Scaling up means choosing a larger size to make a single complex query finish faster. Scaling out adds more clusters of the same size to serve many users at once without queuing. Use scale-up for query complexity and scale-out for concurrency.

scenes.heading: Configuring an elastic warehouse
scenes.code:
CREATE WAREHOUSE analytics_wh
  WAREHOUSE_SIZE = 'MEDIUM'
  AUTO_SUSPEND = 60          -- seconds idle before suspend
  AUTO_RESUME = TRUE
  MIN_CLUSTER_COUNT = 1
  MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT = 4      -- scale out under load
  SCALING_POLICY = 'STANDARD';
scenes.narration: This warehouse starts at Medium size and suspends after sixty idle seconds to save money. Auto-resume brings it back instantly when a query is submitted. Setting the max cluster count to four lets Snowflake add clusters automatically when concurrency spikes.

scenes.heading: How multi-cluster scaling reacts
steps: Clusters shut down as load drops
scenes.narration: When queries begin to queue, the scaling policy launches an additional cluster. Incoming queries are then balanced across all active clusters to keep latency low. As demand falls, Snowflake shuts extra clusters down so you stop paying for idle capacity.

scenes.text: Size up for heavy queries, scale out for concurrency, and lean on auto-suspend to keep the bill honest.
scenes.narration: Match sizing to query complexity, multi-cluster scaling to concurrency, and always let auto-suspend trim idle spend.
